name: Prophet Adam (AS)
title: The First Human & Prophet
summary: The story of the first human being and prophet, created by Allah from clay, and his journey from Paradise to Earth.
content:
Prophet Adam (peace be upon him) was the first human being created by Allah. Allah created him from clay and breathed into him from His spirit. Allah taught Adam the names of all things, knowledge that even the angels did not possess.

Allah commanded the angels to prostrate to Adam as a sign of respect. All the angels obeyed except Iblis (Satan), who refused out of arrogance, saying he was created from fire while Adam was created from clay.

Adam and his wife Hawwa (Eve) lived in Paradise, where they could enjoy everything except one tree. Satan deceived them, and they ate from the forbidden tree. They immediately realized their mistake and felt ashamed.

Allah taught Adam words of repentance, and when Adam sincerely repented, Allah forgave him. However, as a consequence, Adam and Hawwa were sent down to Earth to live and be tested.

Adam became the first prophet, teaching his children about Allah and how to worship Him. He lived for 960 years and had many children who spread across the Earth.
lessons: Allah is the Creator of all things
Knowledge is a great blessing from Allah
Satan is our clear enemy who tries to mislead us
Sincere repentance is always accepted by Allah
We are on Earth to be tested and worship Allah

name: Prophet Nuh (AS)
title: The Patient Caller to Allah
summary: The story of Prophet Noah who called his people to worship Allah alone for 950 years and built the great ark.
content:
Prophet Nuh (Noah) was sent to guide his people who had fallen into idol worship. For 950 years, he patiently called them to worship Allah alone, but most of them rejected his message.

Nuh tried every approach - he called them publicly and privately, during the day and night. He reminded them of Allah's blessings and warned them of His punishment, but they only increased in their rejection.

The disbelievers mocked Nuh and his followers, who were mostly poor and weak people. The chiefs of his people refused to believe, saying they would not follow someone followed by the lowly.

Allah revealed to Nuh that no more of his people would believe. He commanded Nuh to build a great ark (ship). The disbelievers mocked him as he built the ark far from any sea.

When the ark was complete, Allah commanded Nuh to take aboard a pair of every animal and those who believed. Then came the great flood - water gushed from the earth and poured from the sky.

Nuh's own son refused to board the ark and was drowned. The flood destroyed all the disbelievers, and when it ended, the ark rested on Mount Judi. Nuh and the believers were saved, and they became the ancestors of all humanity.
lessons: Patience in calling people to Allah
True nobility is in faith, not wealth or status
Allah's promise always comes true
Family ties don't benefit if there's no faith
Allah saves the believers and destroys the wrongdoers

name: Prophet Ibrahim (AS)
title: The Friend of Allah
summary: The story of Prophet Abraham, the father of prophets, who broke the idols and was willing to sacrifice his son for Allah.
content:
Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) was born among people who worshipped idols. From a young age, he questioned why people worshipped statues they made with their own hands.

Ibrahim challenged his people and even his father Azar, asking them why they worshipped things that couldn't hear, see, or benefit them. When they left for a festival, Ibrahim broke all the idols except the largest one.

When they returned and asked who did this, Ibrahim said, 'Perhaps the big one did it - ask them if they can speak!' They realized their idols were powerless but still refused to believe.

They threw Ibrahim into a huge fire, but Allah commanded the fire: 'Be cool and safe for Ibrahim!' The fire didn't harm him at all.

Ibrahim migrated for Allah's sake and was blessed with two sons - Ismail and Ishaq - in his old age. Allah tested him with the dream to sacrifice his beloved son Ismail. Both father and son submitted to Allah's will, but Allah replaced Ismail with a ram.

Ibrahim and Ismail built the Ka'bah in Makkah, the first house of worship for Allah on Earth. Ibrahim's legacy continued through many prophets from his descendants, including Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon them all).
lessons: Use reason to recognize the truth
Stand firm for truth even if you're alone
Allah protects those who trust in Him
True submission means being ready to sacrifice what we love most
Building places of worship is a great deed

name: Prophet Musa (AS)
title: The One Who Spoke to Allah
summary: The story of Prophet Moses who confronted Pharaoh, parted the Red Sea, and received the Torah from Allah.
content:
Prophet Musa (Moses) was born at a time when Pharaoh was killing all newborn boys of the Israelites. Allah inspired Musa's mother to put him in a basket in the river. Pharaoh's wife found him and raised him in Pharaoh's palace.

As a young man, Musa accidentally killed an Egyptian while defending an Israelite. He fled to Madyan where he married and became a shepherd. One day, he saw a fire on Mount Sinai. When he approached, Allah spoke to him directly and chose him as a prophet.

Allah sent Musa to Pharaoh with clear signs - his staff that turned into a snake, and his hand that shone with white light. Musa asked Pharaoh to free the Israelites and worship Allah alone.

Pharaoh refused and challenged Musa to a contest with his magicians. When the magicians saw Musa's staff swallow all their illusions, they immediately believed in Allah and prostrated, even though Pharaoh threatened to kill them.

Finally, Allah commanded Musa to leave Egypt with the Israelites at night. Pharaoh chased them with his army. When they reached the Red Sea, Allah commanded Musa to strike it with his staff - the sea parted, creating a dry path. The Israelites crossed safely, but when Pharaoh's army followed, the sea closed upon them and they drowned.

Musa received the Torah (Tawrah) from Allah on Mount Sinai and guided his people for many years, though they often disobeyed and tested his patience.
lessons: Allah's plan works in mysterious ways
Truth always prevails over falsehood
Tyrants will eventually be destroyed
Patience with people who disobey
Direct communication with Allah is the highest honor

name: Prophet Isa (AS)
title: The Messiah
summary: The story of Prophet Jesus, born miraculously to Mary, who performed miracles by Allah's permission.
content:
Prophet Isa (Jesus) was born miraculously to Maryam (Mary) without a father. Allah sent the angel Jibreel to Maryam to give her the news of a pure son. She was shocked, but Allah said, 'It is easy for Me.'

When Maryam returned to her people carrying baby Isa, they accused her of wrongdoing. But baby Isa spoke from the cradle, defending his mother and declaring: 'I am the servant of Allah. He has given me the Scripture and made me a prophet.'

As Isa grew, Allah gave him the Injeel (Gospel) and taught him wisdom. He performed many miracles by Allah's permission - healing the blind and the lepers, bringing the dead back to life, and creating a bird from clay that came to life when he breathed into it.

Isa called the Children of Israel to worship Allah alone and follow the law. He gathered disciples who believed in him and supported his message.

The religious leaders of the time rejected Isa and plotted to kill him. But Allah saved Isa and raised him to the heavens. Someone else was made to look like Isa and was crucified instead.

Isa did not die but was raised alive to Allah. He will return before the Day of Judgment to defeat the false messiah (Dajjal) and establish justice on Earth.
lessons: Allah can create without the usual means
Miracles are by Allah's permission, not the prophet's power
Isa was a prophet and servant of Allah, not divine
Allah protects His prophets
Isa will return before the end of times

name: Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ)
title: The Final Messenger
summary: The story of the final prophet sent as a mercy to all of mankind, who received the Quran and established Islam.
content:
Prophet Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon him) was born in Makkah in the year 570 CE. He was known as 'Al-Amin' (the Trustworthy) even before prophethood because of his honesty and good character.

At age 40, while meditating in the cave of Hira, the angel Jibreel came to him with the first revelation: 'Read in the name of your Lord who created.' This was the beginning of the Quran and his prophethood.

The Prophet began calling people to worship Allah alone and abandon idols. The early Muslims faced severe persecution in Makkah. After 13 years, they migrated to Madinah where the first Islamic state was established.

The Prophet led by example in all aspects of life - worship, family relations, business, warfare, and governance. He was merciful even to his enemies, forgiving the people of Makkah when he conquered it peacefully.

In his final sermon during his last pilgrimage, he emphasized the equality of all humans, the rights of women, and the importance of following the Quran and his Sunnah.

The Prophet passed away at age 63, leaving behind the complete religion of Islam, the Quran, and his Sunnah as guidance for all humanity until the Day of Judgment. He is the final prophet - there will be no prophet after him.
lessons: Good character is essential for a believer
Patience and perseverance in the face of hardship
Mercy and forgiveness even toward enemies
Islam is a complete way of life
Following the Prophet's example leads to success
